pencereler.0-5: Two walkways fell onto a crowded hotel lobby in Kansas City. In seconds, one
pencereler.5-12: hundred fourteen people were dead. So how does a walkway just drop? The design used one long rod through
pencereler.12-20: both walkways. During construction, it was swapped for two shorter rods. That quietly doubled the load on one set of nuts. Under
pencereler.20-30: the crowd, the nuts pulled straight through the beam. Now every connection change needs the engineer's approval.

segmentler.metin: The Hyatt Regency walkways collapsed onto a crowded hotel lobby.
It took only a rod change that doubled the load on one connection.
So how could a rod change that doubled the load on one connection do this?
The answer is box-beam connection pull-through from a doubled hanger-rod load — and it is why connection changes during fabrication now need the engineer of record's approval.
